evidence.description: Task launched in initializer without being awaited or handled.

candidates.explanation: The `init` method launches an unawaited `Task` to perform asynchronous work. This can lead to race conditions or unexpected behavior during object initialization, as the object might be used before the initialization work (restoring state) is complete.
candidates.title: Unawaited Task in Initializer

evidence.description: Detached task used to return values to a MainActor-isolated class with explicit MainActor.run calls.

candidates.explanation: The code uses `Task.detached` to perform file I/O and then maps the result to a block that explicitly calls `MainActor.run`. Since the class is already marked with `@MainActor`, the `await Task.detached { ... }.value` pattern combined with an explicit `MainActor.run` inside the map creates unnecessary complexity and potential for confusion regarding actor isolation.
candidates.title: Redundant Actor Isolation Handling

evidence.description: Accessing User.shared.news within a computed property.

candidates.explanation: The `needsUpdate` property accesses `User.shared.news`, which is a global shared state. Accessing shared state inside a computed property can lead to unpredictable results or side effects if the state changes unexpectedly during the evaluation.
candidates.title: Implicit Dependency on Shared State

evidence.description: Concurrent Task creation inside the load method without tracking or canceling previous tasks.

candidates.explanation: The `load` method uses a `Task` block to perform network and decoding operations. If `load` is called multiple times in rapid succession, multiple concurrent tasks will be spawned, potentially leading to out-of-order updates to the `items` set.
candidates.title: Potential Race Condition in Concurrent Loads

evidence.description: String replacement performed via reduce on a dictionary.

candidates.explanation: The `clean` method uses `reduce` to iterate over a dictionary of characters and perform string replacements. This is inefficient as it creates a new string for every entry in the dictionary even if the character is not present.
candidates.title: Inefficient String Processing
